Theme

Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas

undergo verb

also go under, submit to, endure, face (danger), come up to, take upon oneself

classical

Cic. Rosc. Am. 31: omnēs terrōrēs perīculaque omnia succurram atque subībō (Lewis & Short)
Caes. BG 1.36: tēctum nōn subīssent (Lewis & Short)

subeō, subīre, subiī, subitum

verb, irregular (a compound of eō), conjugation

go under; come up to; undergo, take upon oneself

The figure is of stooping under a load: of danger, pain and wrong a favourite expression of Cicero’s (Lewis & Short).

Examples

  • omnēs terrōrēs perīculaque omnia succurram atque subībō

    I will meet every terror and take every danger upon myselfCic. Rosc. Am. 31 (Lewis & Short)

  • quī inter annōs XIV tēctum nōn subīssent

    who had not come under a roof in fourteen yearsCaes. BG 1.36 (Lewis & Short)

See also experience.
